papers_read.title_as_printed: The effects of different types of exercises on cognition in older persons with mild cognitive impairment: A systematic review and meta-analysis (Akalp, Ferreira, Soares, Ribeiro, Teixeira; Archives of Gerontology and Geriatrics 126 (2024) 105541)

Cognitive benefits of music in aerobic exercise: Evidence from a Bayesian network meta-analysis in adults with mild cognitive impairment (Quan, Lo, Wolff, Wang, Olsen, Thompson; Archives of Gerontology and Geriatrics 134 (2025) 105848)

what_each_reports.P-680: Random-effects meta-analysis in CMA 4.0 of 23 controlled exercise studies in MCI (1220 participants). The effect size is a standard difference in means of pre-post change, standardised by change-score SD, with one composite per study combining all its cognitive tests. The 4 studies (259 participants) labelled amnestic MCI were left out of the cognitive analysis. All exercise: SMD 1.165 (95% CI 0.741 to 1.589), Q = 158.930 on 19 df, I2 88.045%, prediction interval -0.747 to 3.077. Aerobic stratum (Amjad 2019, Bademli 2019, Qi 2019, Song & Yu 2019, and Varela 2012 with two arms; df = 5): 1.442. Its 95% CI is printed as 0.642 to 2.260 in Results 3.4 but as 0.624 to 2.260 in the Abstract and Discussion; the prediction interval is -1.440 to 4.324. Resistance: 1.229 (0.339 to 2.120). Multimodal: 0.856 (0.366 to 1.346). No test between exercise types is reported.
what_each_reports.P-683: Multilevel random-effects meta-analysis (Hedges g of change scores, effect sizes nested within study and trial) of 25 RCTs (38 papers, 2048 participants with MCI), with aerobic exercise split by music. Global-cognition domain (MMSE, ADAS-Cog, MoCA, NCSE, NTB) against control: aerobic exercise without music (AEwtM) g = 0.48 [0.18, 0.79] (k = 26 effect sizes, 11 trials, n = 683); aerobic exercise with music (AEwM) g = 1.2 [0.47, 1.94] (2 trials, n = 176); dance g = 0.55 [0.13, 0.96] (6 trials). With high risk-of-bias studies excluded, AEwtM is 0.6 [0.28, 0.93]. The multivariate model's global-cognition estimate is 0.53 [0.16, 0.9] at rho = 0.6 (Appendix E). The NMA estimate for AEwM vs AEwtM on global cognition is 0.73 [-0.09, 1.56], with no direct evidence.

quantity_a: Standardised difference in means of pre-post change for a per-study COMPOSITE of all cognitive tests, comparing exercise with no-exercise control at end of intervention. The trials are controlled (randomised or not) in older adults labelled MCI with the amnestic-labelled trials excluded. For the contested stratum, 'aerobic' is P-680's own class, which includes an aerobic-dance trial and a music-accompanied stepping trial.
quantity_b: Hedges g of pre-post change for the GLOBAL-COGNITION domain only (screening instruments), comparing aerobic exercise WITHOUT music with control at end of intervention. The trials are RCTs of adults aged 50+ with MCI as diagnosed by the original authors, amnestic trials included.
incompatible_if_same: No. Both results favour exercise, both are significant, and the intervals overlap. P-680's aerobic interval (0.642 to 2.260; 0.624 in its abstract) overlaps P-683's 0.18 to 0.79 between 0.642 and 0.79. P-680's all-exercise interval (0.741 to 1.589) overlaps the same range between 0.741 and 0.79, and it also overlaps P-683's multivariate global-cognition interval (0.16 to 0.90). The review's reading counts same-direction results with overlapping intervals as compatible. For transparency, this is my own computation and not the review's test: a normal-approximation test of the difference, treating the two as independent estimates of one parameter, gives z of about 2.2 (aerobic) to 2.6 (all exercise). The two are neither independent (Amjad 2019 and Varela 2012 are in both strata) nor estimates of one quantity.

gates.task: match: T6 vs T6; both are evidence syntheses of exercise efficacy in MCI.
gates.dataset_family: match: both pool published controlled exercise trials in MCI. P-680 covers 23 studies (2012-2023, searched to May 2024); P-683 covers 25 RCTs (2008-2022, searched to 13 January 2023). Six trials appear in both rosters; this is recorded under independence.
gates.validation_tier: n/a: two evidence syntheses, counted as matched.
gates.modality_family: match at the family level (syntheses of exercise interventions with cognitive-test outcomes). The intervention classes inside the family differ; see endpoint_and_metric.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible. The metric type is compatible: both are standardised mean differences of pre-post change. The endpoint and comparison are not. (1) Outcome: P-680 pools one composite per study across all cognitive domains [q6], while P-683 pools the global-cognition domain only [q10]. (2) Intervention class: P-680's aerobic stratum [q7] contains Song & Yu 2019, which P-683 classes as aerobic WITH music [q12], and Qi 2019, which P-683 classes as dance [q13]. P-683's Qi 2018 is the same article (DOI 10.3892/etm.2018.7006) [q14, q15]. Bademli 2019 is in P-680's aerobic stratum but was excluded by P-683 [q16]. Only Amjad 2019 and Varela 2012 fall in P-683's aerobic-without-music node [q17]. (3) Population: P-680 left the amnestic-labelled trials out of its analysis [q3, q4], while P-683's AEwtM node includes amnestic trials, such as the Tarumi 2019 trial and Stuckenschneider 2021, which P-680 labels a-MCI [q17, q22, q23]. The PDF does not list which 11 of P-683's 15 AEwtM trials enter its global-cognition estimate.
performance_validity: Not a performance comparison: these are intervention effect sizes, and neither registry row is flagged.
independence: Not independent in trial content. Six trials appear in both rosters: Varela 2012, Amjad 2019, Song & Yu 2019, Qi 2018/2019 (same article), the Tarumi 2019/Thomas 2020 trial and Stuckenschneider 2021. Two of them, Amjad 2019 and Varela 2012, sit in both contested strata. The author teams differ (Coimbra; Macquarie). P-683 does not cite P-680. P-683 drew its trial pool from its own team's overview of meta-analyses (Quan et al., 2024) plus a database search [q18].
grounds: The two results agree in direction and their intervals overlap: P-680's aerobic 1.442 (0.642 to 2.260) and all-exercise 1.165 (0.741 to 1.589), against P-683's aerobic-without-music 0.48 (0.18 to 0.79). Under Section 5.2 and the brief's reading this is compatibility, the first outcome in the order [q1, q2, q10].

Neither paper claims an ordering that the other refutes. P-680 ranks aerobic and resistance above multimodal exercise without any between-type test. P-683's PICOS excludes resistance and multicomponent exercise, so it tests neither [q19]. P-683's music contrast has no counterpart in P-680 [q9].

Setting the overlap aside would still not make the pair genuine, because the quantities differ. P-680 pools a per-study composite of all cognitive tests, and P-683 pools the global-cognition domain [q6, q10]. P-680's 'aerobic' includes a music-accompanied trial and a dance trial that P-683 assigns to other nodes [q7, q12, q13]. P-680 excludes amnestic-labelled trials, and P-683 includes them [q3, q17].

The record's causal explanation, that P-680's 23 studies are a biomarker-reporting subset, is contradicted by P-680 itself. Its inclusion criterion names blood markers [q5], but the Discussion and Limitations say that only three to four included studies reported them [q8, q20].

record_defects: Conflict statement reason (3) and claim_a say that P-680 admitted studies only if they reported blood markers, so that its 23-study base is 'a biomarker-reporting subset'. P-680 states the criterion [q5], but its Table 2 shows 'NR' in the blood-marker column for most included studies (e.g. [q21]). Its Discussion says three studies with blood markers were included [q8], and its Limitations count four [q20]. The criterion was not applied as a requirement, and the record's leading explanation for the magnitude gap has no basis in the PDF.

The evidence quote attributed to P-683 ('Its global-cognition estimate for aerobic exercise without music (g = 0.48) is also substantially more conservative than P-680's pooled 1.165, which is a useful cross-check suggesting the latter is inflated') does not occur in P-683. P-683 never cites Akalp et al. 2024; this is digest prose.
The conflict statement's 'the same outcome domain (global cognition)' is wrong for P-680, which pools a per-study composite of all cognitive tests [q6], not the global-cognition domain.

'The same intervention family' and the claim that P-680's aerobic stratum and P-683's aerobic-without-music stratum are 'the only like-for-like pair' are both wrong. P-680's aerobic stratum includes Song & Yu 2019 (P-683: with music), Qi 2019 (P-683: dance) and Bademli 2019 (excluded by P-683). Only Amjad 2019 and Varela 2012 are shared with P-683's AEwtM node [q7, q12, q13, q16, q17].

'Neither digest preserves its trial roster, so shared primary trials cannot be excluded.' The PDFs print both rosters (P-680 Table 2; P-683 Appendix G). Six trials are shared, two of them within the contested strata.

The record gives P-680's aerobic CI as 0.642 to 2.260 [q2] without noting that P-680's own abstract and discussion print 0.624 to 2.260 [q1]. This is an internal inconsistency in P-680 and does not change the verdict.
what_would_change_the_verdict: The label could change, but not to genuine. If the adjudicator applies the quantity mismatch before the compatibility test, as in the 2026-09-24 C-234 reclassification (documented incommensurability despite agreeing directions), the verdict becomes documented_incommensurability. A genuine conflict would need a P-680 estimate on the same endpoint and intervention class (global-cognition domain, aerobic exercise without music, amnestic trials handled alike) whose interval excludes P-683's 0.18 to 0.79. Neither PDF reports one.
